prose.title: The Hawks Had No Quarterback in April and Two Starters by August
prose.dek: Chris Klingenberg made no moves in the spring beyond the rookie draft, then spent {{f.team.0012.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, {{f.team.0012.top_buy_price}} of it on Jared Goff. The preseason simulation has the Hawks {{f.team.0012.power_rank|ord}}, in a division with the league's top-ranked team.

paragraphs: April was bare. The Hawks carried {{f.team.0012.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0012.cap_opening}} in salary, and there was no quarterback on the roster at all, so Jakobi Meyers, a receiver, sat in the superflex. Kyren Williams, a High-end RB2, was the only solid starter, and there was not one top-twelve player at any position. The other {{f.team.0012.holes_opening}} spots were holes: nobody at quarterback, J.K. Dobbins at the second running back spot, Mike Evans and Michael Wilson at receiver, Dalton Kincaid at tight end, and RJ Harvey, Chimere Dike and Meyers in the flexes.

Before the rookie draft the Hawks made no moves at all: no trade, no cut, no extension. {{f.team.0012.expired_rookies}} rookie deals ran out and none was kept: Drew Sanders, Luke Schoonmaker and Nolan Smith simply left, and Jordan Battle went to L.A. Looks at the Expired Rookie Auction.

t.0012.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft was the whole pre-auction offseason, and it produced two starters, Carnell Tate and CJ Allen. The Hawks made {{f.team.0012.rookie_picks_count}} picks, two of them in the first round: Carnell Tate at 1.02, a slot that has produced a usable player half the time, and Makai Lemon at 1.06. Tate went straight into the lineup as a Low-end WR3. Kaelon Black, Ja'Kobi Lane and a quarterback, Drew Allar, followed, and CJ Allen is already starting: taken early in the fourth round, he projects as an Elite LB1 on MFL's numbers. Mansoor Delane is in the projected lineup.

No Expired Rookie Auction buys, no tags, no cuts and no trades until the roster locked. Klingenberg went into the auction with {{f.team.0012.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0012.cap_preauction}} in active-roster salary, which left room to spend, and he had a lot to fill.

The Hawks spent {{f.team.0012.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction, and most of it went on the position they did not have. Jared Goff cost {{f.team.0012.faa_12611_price}} after twelve bids, the most contested of his wins, and Matthew Stafford {{f.team.0012.faa_9431_price}}, with Rachaad White at {{f.team.0012.faa_15721_price}}, Rhamondre Stevenson at {{f.team.0012.faa_15259_price}} and Travis Kelce at {{f.team.0012.faa_11244_price}} behind them.

What it bought: Stafford, a Low-end QB1, and Kelce, a Low-end TE1, the two Very good buys; Goff, a High-end QB2 and the Good one, in a superflex league where most lineups carry two quarterbacks; and Stevenson, who starts. White is depth. The league table ranks the Hawks {{f.team.0012.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for how much the auction improved the offense.

The biggest buys signed long: Goff for {{f.team.0012.contract_12611_years}} years at {{f.team.0012.contract_12611_salary}} a year, a TCV of {{f.team.0012.contract_12611_tcv}}, Stafford at {{f.team.0012.contract_9431_tcv}} over two, and White at {{f.team.0012.contract_15721_tcv}}. He made no restructures. After the auction he traded a 2027 fourth to Real Deal Creel for George Karlaftis and a 2027 fifth, a {{f.team.0012.trade1_grade}} from the trade bot, cut Marquise Brown with {{f.team.0012.cut_14105_salary}} of salary and a {{f.team.0012.cut_14105_penalty}} penalty charged to 2027, and claimed a backup kicker, Cairo Santos, and a punter, Sam Martin, off waivers.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0012.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Stafford and Kelce, and {{f.team.0012.holes_today}} holes: Stevenson at the second running back spot, Mike Evans and Carnell Tate at receiver, and Michael Wilson and J.K. Dobbins in the flexes. Receiver is where the Hawks rank lowest, {{f.team.0012.wr_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}. On MFL's projections the defense has a few real starters: CJ Allen is an Elite LB1, and Fred Warner and Chop Robinson grade as a High-end LB2 and a High-end DL2. The kicker, Andres Borregales, is an Elite PK1.

Jakobi Meyers, questionable with a thumb, is in his week one lineup, and the forecast does not sit him. Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah is on injured reserve for the season, and two taxi-squad players are banged up.

t.0012.moves_s3.title: From the auction to week one

captions.t.0012.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is the top three, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter anyone else the league's lineups would start, and Depth the rest.

paragraphs: Klingenberg has been here since {{f.team.0012.hist_first_season}}, {{f.team.0012.hist_seasons}} completed seasons, with no title, one runner-up finish in {{f.team.0012.hist_runner_up_years}}, {{f.team.0012.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, and division titles in 2013 and 2021. His career all-play record of {{f.team.0012.hist_allplay_pct}} is the lowest in the league.

This is year one of the alignment the owners drafted themselves, and Bear Dunn, seated third among the captains, took the Hawks {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0012|ord}} overall, exactly as he had announced in January, the day the draft was first floated. DOG POUND 4 LIFE belongs to C-Town on paper: {{f.league.p_division_0009}} to win it, against {{f.league.p_division_0011}} for Cleon Ca$h and {{f.team.0012.sim_p_division}} for the Hawks, whose playoff odds are {{f.team.0012.sim_p_playoffs}}.

The division weeks are {{f.team.0012.div_weeks}}, with no byes in the first two, and one of them is the worst week on any roster in the division. Week eight costs him Evans and Warner. Week eleven takes five Hawks starters at once, Stafford, Kyren Williams, Stevenson, Borregales and Marcus Jones, against four for C-Town and three for Cleon Ca$h. Week fourteen, the last of the regular season, takes Wilson and DeMarvion Overshown. Across the five weeks he loses {{f.team.0012.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes, C-Town {{f.team.0012.div_week_byes_0009}} and Cleon Ca$h {{f.team.0012.div_week_byes_0011}}.

The next three years, Klingenberg style. 2027: the Hawks win DOG POUND 4 LIFE?!?! Goff and Stafford carry it... no, wait, strike that, C-Town wins it, bro, but the Hawks make the playoffs. 2028: Tate is a lead receiver and Lemon is right behind him, and this is the year, dude, this is definitely the year. It isn't: the Hawks miss the playoffs. 2029: Cleon Ca$h wins the title, out of this very division.

Week one is a division week. With {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Mike Evans caught a touchdown, Kyren Williams ran one in, and the Hawks already have {{f.team.0012.wk_points_final}} points in the bank. Stafford threw an interception in a quiet first game.
